extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, media professionals, and the public interested in journalism ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and newsroom practices for handling plagiarism, attribution, corrections, and disciplinary response in journalism. Focuses on proper attribution, investigative review after allegations, and transparent corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution of sourced material
rubrics_metrics.description: It is The Post’s policy that the use of material from other newspapers or sources must be properly attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles that borrow material from other outlets must include clear attribution to the original source; failure to do so constitutes a policy breach and should be corrected publicly (for example, with an editor's note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism is a cardinal sin in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is described as 'one of the cardinal sins in journalism.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting another outlet’s work as your own is unacceptable. The reporter's apology states: 'I used another newspaper’s work as if it were my own. It was wrong. It was inexcusable. And it is one of the cardinal sins in journalism.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines do not excuse plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the pressure of tight deadlines is not an acceptable justification for using another newspaper’s work as if it were one’s own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when facing tight deadlines, journalists must not reuse others' text without attribution; remorse and apology do not negate the breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionate disciplinary action reflecting seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action should be 'appropriately severe and reflects the seriousness with which we view this transgression,' per the executive editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should apply sanctions that match the severity of the violation (examples include suspension) and communicate that judgement internally and, where appropriate, publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct an editorial review/audit after allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors conducted a review of all of Horwitz’s published work this year and reviewed dozens of earlier stories to check for other evidence of plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After an allegation, news organizations should perform a systematic review of the reporter’s recent and past work to determine whether the issue is isolated or systemic, and report findings publicly when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public correction and editorial note for affected stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Both stories are now prefaced with this note: 'This is one of two articles published by The Post online and in its print editions earlier this month that contained substantial material that was borrowed and duplicated, without attribution, from The Arizona Republic newspaper.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When plagiarism is confirmed, affected articles should be clearly prefaced or amended with an editor's note explaining the issue; apologies to readers and the original outlet should be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apologize to readers, colleagues, and affected outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporter issued an apology: 'I am deeply sorry. To our readers, my friends and colleagues, my editors, and to the paper I love, I want to apologize.' The Post apologized to The Arizona Republic and its readers for the lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public, specific apology is expected when wrongdoing involves misappropriation of another outlet’s work; it should acknowledge the wrongdoing and its inappropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take allegations from peer outlets seriously and act on them
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post was alerted to the plagiarism by Republic editor Randy Lovely and then investigated and responded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should treat credible alerts from other publications as triggers for prompt investigation, correction, and, if needed, discipline.
